transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

That symptom is very likely from the boil-over: Er03 on AEG induction hobs usually means the touch-control area is being continuously activated, commonly by water, starch residue, a pan/cloth over the controls, or moisture that has got beneath the glass edge. The hob shuts down as a safety measure.

What to do:

1. Turn the hob off at the mains/isolation switch or circuit breaker — don’t just use the touch Off control.
2. Remove pans and wipe up all liquid, especially around and over the front touch-control strip and glass edges.
3. Clean away any sticky pasta-water/starch residue with a barely damp cloth, then dry thoroughly.
4. Leave it powered off for at least 30–60 minutes. If a lot boiled over or liquid may have run into the control area, leave it off for several hours / overnight to dry.
5. Restore power and try again, ensuring nothing is resting on the controls.

Do not keep trying to operate it while it is beeping or showing the error, and don’t use a hairdryer or force heat into the control area.

If Er03 returns after it has fully dried and the control area is clean and empty, keep it isolated and arrange an AEG appliance engineer/electrician visit. Water may have reached the touch-control electronics, particularly if liquid ran down the front edge or underneath the hob.

Tried it. There was starchy water across the slider, so I wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for about 5 minutes. It's working again now, and I moved a wooden spoon that was resting on the edge. Is that all I need to do?

Probably, yes — the starchy water on the slider was the most likely cause, and moving anything resting on/near the controls was sensible. Er03 is generally the hob detecting a continuously “pressed” touch control.

Since it is now operating normally:

• Give the whole control strip another wipe with a clean damp cloth to remove any starch film, then dry it well.
• Keep the slider/control area clear while cooking; even a damp wooden spoon, wet cloth, pan handle, or spill can sometimes be detected as a touch.
• Watch for any repeat beeping/error over the next few uses.

Five minutes off was enough to reset it, but if liquid got under the glass it may take longer to dry. If Er03 comes back when the surface is clean, dry, and completely clear, switch it off at the wall and leave it isolated for several hours or overnight. If it still recurs after that, arrange service rather than continuing to use it.
